goal: Fix the reproduced Windows Cursor reviewer transport defect where a large review prompt is passed through agent.cmd as a positional command-line argument and fails with 'The command line is too long.' Preserve the same read-only reviewer authority and structured envelope semantics while moving only the reviewer prompt transport to stdin.
acceptance_conditions: A deterministic regression reproduces the pre-fix Windows-wrapper risk with a reviewer prompt longer than 8191 characters and proves the fixed reviewer argv no longer contains the prompt text
real_cursor_reviewer_invoker transports the prompt through stdin rather than a positional command-line argument
Cursor reviewer authority remains read-only: --mode ask and --trust/workspace behavior preserved; --force and --yolo remain absent
reviewer output-format json and strict stdout-only provider-envelope parsing remain unchanged
stderr remains diagnostic-only and nonzero reviewer exits still fail closed
builder prompt transport and Claude session-recovery behavior remain unchanged
the subprocess helper change, if needed, is backward-compatible for all existing callers and does not introduce shell=True
short reviewer prompts and long reviewer prompts both preserve exact prompt bytes/characters through stdin in deterministic tests
python scripts/verify_assurance_baseline.py reports ALL PHASES PASSED
independent Cursor adversarial review returns SAFE
stop_conditions: a reliable fix would require broad controller redesign, new external dependencies, shell=True, reviewer write authority, or weakening strict structured-result validation
the repair would require changing Claude builder transport or session recovery rather than only the shared subprocess helper/reviewer boundary needed for stdin
the repair would require modifying governance, job logic, Candidate Truth, immigration doctrine, or resume/package logic
stdin transport cannot be proven to preserve exact reviewer prompt content and strict output parsing
